answer.summary: Power of a one-sided one-sample t-test to detect a 0.2-unit mean increase with SD 0.5, significance level α=0.05, and n=25 participants is 0.6173 (approximately 61.7%).
answer.method: One-sided one-sample t-test using non-central t distribution. Power calculated as P(T > t_crit | H₁) where T ~ t(df=24, noncentrality parameter δ = Cohen's d × √n = 0.4 × 5 = 2.0), and t_crit is the upper-tail critical value at α=0.05.
assumptions: One-sided test with null hypothesis H₀: μ ≤ 0 and alternative H₁: μ > 0
Significance level α = 0.05 (two-tailed critical value applied to one tail)
limitations: Power calculation assumes the assumed SD = 0.5 is the true population standard deviation; if actual SD differs, achieved power will differ
No assumption of unequal variances or robust methods; standard t-test theory applies
One-sided test assumes the direction of the effect (increase) is specified a priori

# One-sided one-sample t-test power calculation
# H0: μ ≤ 0 vs H1: μ > 0
# Parameters:
n <- 25                 # Sample size (participants)
delta <- 0.2            # Mean difference to detect
sigma <- 0.5            # Standard deviation
alpha <- 0.05           # Significance level
sidedness <- "one.sided" # One-sided test

# Cohen's d effect size
cohens_d <- delta / sigma

# Noncentrality parameter
ncp <- cohens_d * sqrt(n)

# Degrees of freedom
df <- n - 1

# Critical t-value (one-sided, upper tail)
t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha, df)

# Power: P(T > t_crit | H1 is true)
# Under H1, T ~ t(df, ncp)
power <- 1 - pt(t_crit, df, ncp = ncp)

cat("One-Sample t-Test Power Calculation\n")
cat("====================================\n")
cat(sprintf("Sample size (n):              %d participants\n", n))
cat(sprintf("Mean difference (δ):          %.2f units\n", delta))
cat(sprintf("Standard deviation (σ):       %.2f units\n", sigma))
cat(sprintf("Cohen's d:                    %.2f\n", cohens_d))
cat(sprintf("Noncentrality parameter:      %.2f\n", ncp))
cat(sprintf("Significance level (α):       %.3f\n", alpha))
cat(sprintf("Degrees of freedom:           %d\n", df))
cat(sprintf("Critical t-value (one-sided): %.4f\n", t_crit))
cat(sprintf("Power (1 - β):                %.6f\n", power))

# Return result in required format
result <- data.frame(
  metric = "power",
  value = power,
  unit = "probability"
)

cat("\n")
print(result)

# Store for verification
writeLines(sprintf("%.15f", power), "power_result.txt")
